[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Solve the expression using the **BODMAS** rule by processing the bracket and multiplication first.

87 − 43 + 92 − (55) + 82

Group positive and negative terms: (87 + 92 + 82) − (43 + 55)

261 − 98 = 163

**∴ The correct answer is 163.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** 87 − 43 + 92 − (38 + 17) + 41 × 2

**Formula Used:** **BODMAS** (Brackets, Orders, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction)

⇒ Solve the **bracket** part: (38 + 17) = 55

⇒ Perform the **multiplication**: 41 × 2 = 82

⇒ The expression becomes: 87 − 43 + 92 − 55 + 82

⇒ Perform **addition** of positive terms: 87 + 92 + 82 = 261

⇒ Perform **addition** of negative terms: 43 + 55 = 98

⇒ Final **subtraction**: 261 − 98 = 163

**∴ The correct answer is 163.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule

It defines the order of operations: **B**rackets, **O**f (powers/roots), **D**ivision, **M**ultiplication, **A**ddition, and **S**ubtraction.

Grouping Technique

When dealing with multiple addition and subtraction terms, summing all positive numbers and all negative numbers separately before the final subtraction reduces calculation errors.

questions.question: Evaluate: [(a + b)⁵ - (a - b)³] ÷ (4ab) for a = 2, b = 5
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Substitute **a = 2** and **b = 5** directly into the expression.

(a + b)⁵ = 7⁵ = **16807** and (a − b)³ = (−3)³ = **−27**.

Numerator = 16807 − (−27) = 16807 + 27 = **16834**.

Denominator = 4 × 2 × 5 = **40**.

Expression = 16834 ÷ 40 = **420.85**.

**∴ The correct answer is 420.85.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Variable **a = 2**

Variable **b = 5**

**Expression to evaluate:** [(a + b)⁵ − (a − b)³] ÷ (4ab)

**Step-by-step Calculation:**

⇒ First, find the values of (a + b) and (a − b):

⇒ (a + b) = 2 + 5 = **7**

⇒ (a − b) = 2 − 5 = **−3**

⇒ Calculate the powers:

⇒ (7)⁵ = 7 × 7 × 7 × 7 × 7 = **16807**

⇒ (−3)³ = (−3) × (−3) × (−3) = **−27**

⇒ Substitute these into the numerator:

⇒ Numerator = 16807 − (−27) = 16807 + 27 = **16834**

⇒ Calculate the denominator:

⇒ 4ab = 4 × 2 × 5 = **40**

⇒ Divide the numerator by the denominator:

⇒ Result = 16834 ÷ 40 = **420.85**

**∴ The correct answer is 420.85.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule

This rule dictates the order of operations: **Brackets**, **Of**, **Division**, **Multiplication**, **Addition**, and **Subtraction**.

Negative Base Exponents

A negative base raised to an **odd power** remains negative, e.g., (−x)³ = −x³, while an **even power** makes it positive, e.g., (−x)² = x².

Powers of 7

Knowing common powers like 7² = 49, 7³ = 343, 7⁴ = 2401, and 7⁵ = 16807 helps in quick **simplification**.

questions.question: Which of the following is greater than (13/24)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Convert the base fraction **13/24** into its **decimal** equivalent: 13 ÷ 24 ≈ **0.5416**.

Compare the decimal values of the given options:

(1) 26/51 ≈ 0.509 | (2) 27/50 = 0.540 | (4) 7/13 ≈ 0.538

(3) 25/46 ≈ **0.5434**

Since **0.5434** is greater than **0.5416**, the fraction **25/46** is the largest.

**∴ The correct answer is 25/46.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Base fraction = **13/24**

**Method:** We use the **cross-multiplication** rule to compare fractions. For two fractions **a/b** and **c/d**, if **a × d > b × c**, then **a c/d**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e34b5de396566381717b676e2b8622d9a113a713dbe7ec38786e5cdc2bb8cd76.png] 

**Step-by-step Comparison:**

⇒ Comparing **13/24** and **26/51**: 13 × 51 = 663 and 24 × 26 = 624. Since 663 > 624 ⇒ **13/24 > 26/51**.

⇒ Comparing **13/24** and **27/50**: 13 × 50 = 650 and 24 × 27 = 648. Since 650 > 648 ⇒ **13/24 > 27/50**.

⇒ Comparing **13/24** and **25/46**: 13 × 46 = 598 and 24 × 25 = 600. Since 600 > 598 ⇒ **25/46 > 13/24**.

⇒ Comparing **13/24** and **7/13**: 13 × 13 = 169 and 24 × 7 = 168. Since 169 > 168 ⇒ **13/24 > 7/13**.

**∴ The correct answer is 25/46.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Cross-Multiplication Rule

questions.question: frac{0.25 × 0.25 + 0.015} {0.2 × 0.2 + 0.01} = ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Solve the numerator and denominator separately using **basic arithmetic**.

Numerator = (0.25 × 0.25) + 0.015 = 0.0625 + 0.015 = 0.0775.

Denominator = (0.2 × 0.2) + 0.01 = 0.04 + 0.01 = 0.05.

Result = 0.0775 ÷ 0.05 = 7.75 ÷ 5 = 1.55.

**∴ The correct answer is 1.55.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** (0.25 × 0.25 + 0.015) ÷ (0.2 × 0.2 + 0.01)

**Method Used:** BODMAS and Decimal Simplification

⇒ (0.0625 + 0.015) ÷ (0.04 + 0.01)

⇒ 0.0775 ÷ 0.05

⇒ 775/10000 ÷ 5/100

⇒ 775/10000 × 100/5

⇒ 775 ÷ (100 × 5)

⇒ 775 ÷ 500

⇒ 1.55

**∴ The correct answer is 1.55.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule

Always prioritize **Multiplication** before **Addition** as per the rule: Brackets, Orders, Division/Multiplication, Addition/Subtraction.

Decimal Multiplication

When multiplying **decimals**, the result contains a number of decimal places equal to the sum of decimal places in the multipliers (e.g., 0.25 × 0.25 = 0.0625).

Simplification Tip

To divide by 0.05, multiply the numerator by 100 and then divide by 5 to simplify **fractional calculations**.

questions.question: What is the remainder when 1200 is divided by 9?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **remainder** of any number when divided by **9** is equal to the **sum of its digits** (reduced to a single digit if necessary).

For the number 1200, the **sum of digits** = 1 + 2 + 0 + 0 = 3.

Since 3 is less than 9, the **remainder** is 3.

**∴ The correct answer is 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Dividend** = 1200, **Divisor** = 9

**Formula:** Dividend = (Divisor × Quotient) + Remainder

⇒ 1200 ÷ 9

⇒ 1200 = 1197 + 3

⇒ 1200 = (9 × 133) + 3

⇒ Quotient = 133

⇒ **Remainder** = 3

**∴ The correct answer is 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Divisibility Rule of 9

A number is perfectly divisible by 9 if and only if the **sum of its digits** is divisible by 9. This sum also determines the remainder for non-divisible numbers.

Concept of Digital Root

The **digital root** is the single-digit value obtained by repeatedly adding digits until a single digit remains. If the digital root is 9, the remainder is 0; otherwise, the digital root is the **remainder** when divided by 9.

Divisibility Rule of 3

Similar to 9, a number is divisible by 3 if the **sum of its digits** is divisible by 3. For 1200, 1+2+0+0 = 3, which is divisible by 3, so the remainder when divided by 3 is 0.

questions.question: A square park has sides of length 15 cm. A, 3 cm wide path is inside it. What is the area (in square cm) of the path?
questions.solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ For a **square park** of side **s** having an **inside path** of width **w**: **Area of Path = 4w(s − w)** Given **s = 15 cm** and **w = 3 cm**: Area = 4 × 3 × (15 − 3) = 12 × 12 = 144 cm² **∴ The correct answer is 144 cm².**

questions.question: The perimeter of a rectangle is 50 cm. The length of the rectangle is 15 cm. What is the area (in square cm) of the rectangle?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In a **Rectangle**, the sum of **Length** and **Breadth** is always half of the **Perimeter**.

L + B = 50 ÷ 2 = 25 cm.

Since L = 15 cm, B = 25 − 15 = 10 cm.

**Area** = L × B = 15 × 10 = 150 cm².

**∴ The correct answer is 150 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Perimeter** of the rectangle = 50 cm

**Length** (L) of the rectangle = 15 cm

**Formula Used:**

**Perimeter** = 2 × (Length + Breadth)

**Area** = Length × Breadth

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/968b594966d3470a45bd86d2d229eabeb4b4d0fa93eec106dbc7a2997066f5c5.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 2 × (15 + B) = 50

⇒ 15 + B = 50 ÷ 2

⇒ 15 + B = 25

⇒ B = 25 − 15

⇒ B = 10 cm

Now, calculate the **Area**:

⇒ **Area** = 15 × 10

⇒ **Area** = 150 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 150 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Diagonal of a Rectangle

The distance between opposite corners is given by d = √(L² + B²).

Properties of Rectangle

Opposite sides are equal and parallel, and every internal angle is exactly 90°.

Circumradius of a Rectangle

The radius of a circle passing through all vertices is half of the diagonal: R = d ÷ 2.

questions.question: The perimeter of a rectangle is 40 cm. The length of the rectangle is 12 cm. What is the sum (in cm) of length and breadth of the rectangle?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **perimeter** of a **rectangle** is twice the **sum** of its **length** and **breadth**.

Sum of (Length + Breadth) = Perimeter ÷ 2

Sum = 40 ÷ 2 = 20 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 20 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Perimeter** = 40 cm, **Length** = 12 cm

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9563fd8e6d8624dc2606a2e65e54a8f1113d75823395931313edc517fead07d2.png] 

**Formula Used:** **Perimeter** = 2 × (**Length** + **Breadth**)

⇒ 40 = 2 × (12 + **Breadth**)

⇒ 12 + **Breadth** = 40 ÷ 2

⇒ 12 + **Breadth** = 20

⇒ **Breadth** = 20 − 12 = 8 cm

⇒ **Sum** of length and breadth = 12 + 8 = 20 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 20 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of a Rectangle

The total space occupied by a **rectangle** is the product of its **length** and **breadth**: Area = Length × Breadth.

Diagonal of a Rectangle

The **diagonal** (d) is the longest line segment connecting opposite corners: d = √(Length² + Breadth²).

Perimeter of a Square

A **square** is a special rectangle where length = breadth = side (a). Its **perimeter** is 4 × a.

questions.question: If x = frac{3+sqrt{8}}{3-sqrt{8}} , y = frac{3-sqrt{8}}{3+sqrt{8}} , then what is the value of x² + y²?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Notice that **x** and **y** are **reciprocal conjugates** ($xy = 1$).

For $x = \frac{a+b}{a-b}$ and $y = \frac{a-b}{a+b}$, the sum $x+y = \frac{2(a²+b²)}{a²-b²}$.

Substitute $a=3$ and $b=\sqrt{8}$: $x+y = \frac{2(9+8)}{9-8} = 34$.

Applying the identity $x² + y² = (x + y)² − 2xy$.

Calculation: $34² − 2(1) = 1156 − 2 = 1154$.

**∴ The correct answer is 1154.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

x = (3 + √8) ÷ (3 − √8)

y = (3 − √8) ÷ (3 + √8)

**Formula Used:**

x² + y² = (x + y)² − 2xy

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Rationalizing** x: x = [(3 + √8) × (3 + √8)] ÷ [(3 − √8) × (3 + √8)] ⇒ x = (9 + 8 + 6√8) ÷ (9 − 8) = 17 + 6√8 ⇒ **Rationalizing** y: y = [(3 − √8) × (3 − √8)] ÷ [(3 + √8) × (3 − √8)] ⇒ y = (9 + 8 − 6√8) ÷ (9 − 8) = 17 − 6√8 ⇒ x + y = (17 + 6√8) + (17 − 6√8) = 34 ⇒ xy = [(3 + √8) ÷ (3 − √8)] × [(3 − √8) ÷ (3 + √8)] = 1 ⇒ x² + y² = 34² − 2(1) ⇒ x² + y² = 1156 − 2 = 1154

**∴ The correct answer is 1154.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Rationalization of Surds

To rationalize a denominator, multiply both numerator and denominator by the **conjugate** of the denominator to eliminate the radical.

Algebraic Identity for Sum of Squares

The **sum of squares** identity is x² + y² = (x + y)² − 2xy, which is extremely useful when the product xy is a simple integer like 1.

Reciprocal Conjugates

If the difference of the squares of two terms in a binomial surd is 1 (e.g., 3² − (√8)² = 1), then the expression and its conjugate are **multiplicative inverses**.

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Identify the **number of terms (n)**: n = [(Last − First) ÷ Diff] + 1 = [(203 − 31) ÷ 2] + 1 = 87.

Find the **average** of the series: (First + Last) ÷ 2 = (31 + 203) ÷ 2 = 117.

**Total Sum** = Average × n = 117 × 87 = 10179.

**∴ The correct answer is 10179.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** The series is an **Arithmetic Progression (AP)** with first term **a = 31**, last term **l = 203**, and common difference **d = 2**.

**Formula Used:** Sum Sₙ = (n ÷ 2) × (a + l) and n = [(l − a) ÷ d] + 1.

⇒ First, calculate the **number of terms (n)**:

⇒ n = [(203 − 31) ÷ 2] + 1

⇒ n = [172 ÷ 2] + 1 = 86 + 1 = 87

⇒ Now, calculate the **sum (Sₙ)**:

⇒ Sₙ = (87 ÷ 2) × (31 + 203)

⇒ Sₙ = (87 ÷ 2) × 234

⇒ Sₙ = 87 × 117 = 10179

**∴ The correct answer is 10179.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sum of First n Odd Natural Numbers

The sum of the first n **odd natural numbers** starting from 1 is given by the formula: Sₙ = n².

General Term of an AP

The **nth term** of an Arithmetic Progression is defined as: aₙ = a + (n − 1)d.

Alternate Sum Formula

The sum of an AP can also be calculated as: Sₙ = (n ÷ 2)[2a + (n − 1)d].

questions.question: The average of three values is 30. First value is 1/3 of the third value. Third value is 15 more than second value. What is the first value?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Total Sum** of three values = 30 × 3 = 90.

Ratio logic: Let the **Third value** = 3 units, so the **First value** = 1 unit.

The **Second value** = 3 units − 15.

Total units: 1 + 3 + (3 − 15) = 90 ⇒ 7 units = 105.

1 unit = 105 ÷ 7 = 15.

**∴ The correct answer is 15.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Average** of three values = 30

**First value** = 1/3 of the **Third value**

**Third value** = **Second value** + 15

**Formula Used:**

**Sum** = **Average** × **Total Number of Values**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/686d66fab7ef004bf0dbdbb220c551babaea6847450179a65317bdf5ea331d52.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Total Sum** = 30 × 3 = 90

⇒ Let the **Third value** be x.

⇒ **First value** = x/3

⇒ **Second value** = x − 15

⇒ x/3 + (x − 15) + x = 90

⇒ x/3 + 2x − 15 = 90

⇒ x/3 + 2x = 105

⇒ (x + 6x) / 3 = 105

⇒ 7x = 315

⇒ x = 315 ÷ 7 = 45

⇒ **First value** = 45 ÷ 3 = 15

**∴ The correct answer is 15.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Basic Average Formula

The **Average** of n observations is calculated as the **Sum** of all observations divided by the total number of observations (n).

Relationship between Sum and Average

Total **Sum** = **Average** × Total number of entities. This is the most common starting point for solving word problems involving averages.

Ratio and Proportion in Averages

When values are linked by ratios (like 1/3), it is often easier to assign 'units' (e.g., 1x and 3x) to avoid complex fractions during **algebraic substitution**.

questions.question: What is the smallest number which when increased by 30 is exactly divisible by 6, 10 and 12?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

To find the **smallest number**, we first calculate the **Least Common Multiple (LCM)** of the given divisors.

**LCM** of 6, 10, and 12 = 60.

Since the number is **increased by 30** to be divisible, the original number is LCM − 30.

Required Number = 60 − 30 = 30.

**∴ The correct answer is 30.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Divisors = 6, 10, 12

Amount increased = 30

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/50dbf0c2dc2db1d8ccbf32203b4970060e30341c0c80a526591d9cf1eb64dd56.png] 

To find the **LCM** of 6, 10, and 12:

⇒ Prime factors of 6 = 2 × 3

⇒ Prime factors of 10 = 2 × 5

⇒ Prime factors of 12 = 2² × 3

⇒ **LCM** = 2² × 3 × 5 = 4 × 3 × 5 = 60

Let the required number be **x**.

According to the problem, when **x** is increased by 30, it becomes a multiple of 60.

⇒ x + 30 = 60

⇒ x = 60 − 30

⇒ x = 30

**∴ The correct answer is 30.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

LCM Concept

The **Least Common Multiple** is the smallest positive integer that is perfectly divisible by every number in a given set.

General Form for Increased/Decreased Numbers

If a number **N** is increased by **k** to be divisible by **a, b, c**, then N = LCM(a, b, c) − k. If decreased by **k**, then N = LCM(a, b, c) + k.

Divisibility Rule for 12

A number is exactly divisible by **12** if it satisfies the divisibility rules for both **3** (sum of digits divisible by 3) and **4** (last two digits divisible by 4).

questions.question: What is the least number, which when divided by 9, 16, 30 and 24 leaves remainder 6 in each case?
questions.solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ The **least number** that leaves a **common remainder** when divided by several numbers is given by: **LCM** (Divisors) + **Remainder**. Divisors: 9, 16, 30, 24 | Common Remainder: 6 LCM(9, 16, 30, 24) = 720 Required Number = 720 + 6 = 726 **∴ The correct answer is 726.**

questions.question: A person donates 30 percent of his income and deposits 50 percent of the remainder in his bank. If the remaining amount is Rs. 3500 now, then what is the income of the person?
questions.solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ Let the **Total Income** be I. Remaining amount fraction = I × (100 − 30)% × (100 − 50)% = 3500 I × 0.70 × 0.50 = 3500 I × 0.35 = 3500 I = 3500 ÷ 0.35 = 10000 **∴ The correct answer is Rs. 10000.**

questions.question: Ratio of the value of loss incurred on an article to the selling price of the article is 7 : 11. What is the loss percentage?

questions.question: Ratio of the value of loss incurred on an article to the selling price of the article is 5 : 7. What is the loss percentage?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Loss** to **Selling Price** = 5 : 7.

**Cost Price** = **Selling Price** + **Loss** = 7 + 5 = 12 units.

**Loss Percentage** = (**Loss** ÷ **Cost Price**) × 100.

**Loss Percentage** = (5 ÷ 12) × 100 = 41.67%.

**∴ The correct answer is 41.67 percent.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of **Loss** to **Selling Price (SP)** = 5 : 7.

**Formula Used:**

1. **Cost Price (CP)** = **Selling Price (SP)** + **Loss**

2. **Loss Percentage** = (**Loss** ÷ **Cost Price**) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3a9479d7475241ccbcb5df9421b4d3b54eedbf0ca1939d3498a0242fea51dcd.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let **Loss** = 5x and **Selling Price** = 7x.

⇒ **Cost Price (CP)** = 7x + 5x = 12x.

⇒ **Loss %** = (5x ÷ 12x) × 100.

⇒ **Loss %** = (5 ÷ 12) × 100 = 41.666...

⇒ **Loss %** ≈ 41.67%.

**∴ The correct answer is 41.67 percent.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit Percentage

Profit occurs when **Selling Price** > **Cost Price**. Formula: Profit % = [(SP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100.

Marked Price and Discount

Discount is always calculated on the **Marked Price (MP)**. SP = MP − Discount. Discount % = (Discount ÷ MP) × 100.

Relationship between CP and SP

In case of **Loss**, SP = CP × (100 − Loss%) ÷ 100. In case of **Profit**, SP = CP × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100.

questions.question: A pipe can fill a tank in 80 minutes. In how much time (in seconds) can it fill 25 percent of the tank?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total time for **100%** filling = **80 min**

Time for **25%** filling = 80 ÷ 4 = **20 min**

Convert to **seconds**: 20 × 60 = **1200 sec**

**∴ The correct answer is 1200 sec.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time to fill full tank = **80 min**

Target portion = **25%**

**Formula:**

Required Time = Total Time × Required fraction

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/24cf45306c86990c191636d5fe500f15f1c63ae21290226cdb209c6370870b04.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total time in seconds = 80 × 60 = 4800 sec

⇒ 25% of the total time = (25 ÷ 100) × 4800

⇒ Required time = 1/4 × 4800

⇒ Required time = 1200 sec

**∴ The correct answer is 1200 sec.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Time and Work Relation

The time taken to complete a part of a work is directly proportional to the size of that part. **Time = Work ÷ Efficiency**.

Percentage to Fraction Conversion

To convert **percentage** to **fraction**, divide by 100. For example, 25% = 25/100 = 1/4.

Unit Conversion

To convert **minutes** to **seconds**, multiply by 60 (1 min = 60 sec). To convert **seconds** to **minutes**, divide by 60.

questions.question: A car covers a distance of 12 km in 36 minutes. If its speed is decreased by 8 km/hr, then what will be the time (in minutes) taken by it to cover the same distance?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Initial Speed = 12 ÷ (36/60) = 20 km/hr.

New Speed = 20 − 8 = 12 km/hr.

Since **Distance** is constant, Speed ratio 20 : 12 = 5 : 3 → Time ratio = 3 : 5.

3 units = 36 min ⇒ 1 unit = 12 min ⇒ 5 units = 60 min.

**∴ The correct answer is 60 min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Distance** = 12 km, **Initial Time** = 36 min, **Speed Decrease** = 8 km/hr.

**Formula Used:** Speed = Distance ÷ Time | Time = Distance ÷ Speed

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b44de258f56862bcabb96e97450a728849c600761960c59c243ce90fc33c62ef.png] 

⇒ **Initial Time** in hours = 36 ÷ 60 = 0.6 hours.

⇒ **Initial Speed** = 12 ÷ 0.6 = 20 km/hr.

⇒ **New Speed** = 20 − 8 = 12 km/hr.

⇒ **New Time** = 12 ÷ 12 = 1 hour.

⇒ **New Time** in minutes = 1 × 60 = 60 min.

**∴ The correct answer is 60 min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relationship between Speed, Time, and Distance

When **Distance** is constant, **Speed** is inversely proportional to **Time** (S₁/S₂ = T₂/T₁).

Unit Conversion

To convert **km/hr** to **m/s**, multiply by 5/18. To convert **m/s** to **km/hr**, multiply by 18/5.

Average Speed

If a certain distance is covered at **x km/hr** and the same distance at **y km/hr**, the **Average Speed** = (2 × x × y) ÷ (x + y).

questions.question: Total marked price of 600 articles is Rs. 450. 40 percent discount is given. What will be the selling price for 18000 such articles? (marked price of each article is same)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of articles = 18000 ÷ 600 = 30 times.

Total **Marked Price** for 18000 articles = 450 × 30 = ₹13500.

Since a 40% **discount** is given, **Selling Price** = 60% of Total MP.

Total SP = 60% of 13500 = 0.6 × 13500 = ₹8100.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹8100.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total **Marked Price** (MP) of 600 articles = ₹450

Total articles to find SP for = 18000

**Discount** percentage = 40%

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = MP − Discount

SP = MP × (100 − Discount %)/100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0c0447debc860c9d71ccf2e4ca17d88e1472f90c8ad964c45f7e9f773386777c.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ MP of 1 article = 450 ÷ 600 = ₹0.75

⇒ MP of 18000 articles = 18000 × 0.75

⇒ MP of 18000 articles = ₹13500

⇒ Discount on 18000 articles = 40% of 13500

⇒ Discount = (40/100) × 13500 = ₹5400

⇒ Selling Price = Total MP − Discount

⇒ Selling Price = 13500 − 5400 = ₹8100

**∴ The correct answer is ₹8100.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price (MP)

It is the price printed on the article or the price at which the retailer intends to sell the product before offering any discount.

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts of d1% and d2% are given, the equivalent single discount is given by (d1 + d2 − (d1 × d2)/100)%.

Profit and Loss Relation

The relationship between CP and MP is given by: CP/MP = (100 − Discount%)/(100 + Profit%).
